mathematical_errata.original_caption: LHS was sum_i||A_rho^(-1/2)M_ei f||_2^2 but RHS carried an extra input factor 1/(rho^2+|eta|^2).
mathematical_errata.corrected_derivation: Let J_{rho,eps}(eta)=int e^{-eps|xi|^2} mu(dxi)/(rho^2+|eta+xi|^2). With H_i=A_rho^(-1/2) M_ei A_rho^(-1/2), the two correct Gaussian/Plancherel identities are: (A) unweighted-input/output-half-weight: sum_i||A_rho^(-1/2) M_ei g||_2^2 = (2pi)^{-d} int |g-hat(eta)|^2 J_{rho,eps}(eta) d eta, with NO extra (rho^2+|eta|^2) in the denominator; (B) sandwich with BOTH half-weights: put U=A_rho^(-1/2) f, so sum_i||H_i f||_2^2 = sum_i||A_rho^(-1/2) M_ei U||_2^2 = (2pi)^{-d} int |f-hat(eta)|^2 /(rho^2+|eta|^2) * J_{rho,eps}(eta) d eta. Using J<=R_alpha rho^{alpha-2} (source 037 resolvent) and 1/(rho^2+|eta|^2)<=rho^{-2} gives sum_i||H_i f||^2 <= R_alpha rho^{alpha-2} * rho^{-2} ||f||^2 = R_alpha rho^{alpha-4}||f||^2, i.e. the balanced quadratic-form bound sum_i H_i^2 <= R_alpha rho^{alpha-4} I. H_i is selfadjoint (A_rho^{-1/2}, M_ei, A_rho^{-1/2} all selfadjoint) so the row sum H_i^2 and the column sum coincide. The Hermite Fock roles are unchanged: creation row sqrt(N+1), annihilation sqrt(N), sum 2 sqrt(N+1), hence d_N=2 sqrt(N+1) sqrt(R_alpha).
mathematical_errata.why_restore_half_weight: Restoring the input A_rho^{-1/2} on f (so the object is A_rho^{-1/2} M_ei A_rho^{-1/2}, exactly source 5258-5269) is the correct repair, not a change of d_N or the source statement: the input half-weight is precisely what turns the resolvent power rho^{alpha-2} into the sandwich power rho^{alpha-4}, and d_N is the norm of that sandwich. At rho=2 the erroneous returned RHS has denominator bounded by 1/4, so it is at most one quarter of the stated positive LHS (nonzero covariance, nonzero f); the single-half-weight identity (A) has no such extra factor.

Derive the source bound: for free Schwartz data w0 with z(t)=S0(t)w0, d/dt ||z(t)||_rho^2 = 2 rho^2 Re <A_rho^(-1) ̇w0, w0>, and |2 rho^2 Re<A_rho^(-1)̇w0,w0>| <= rho ||z(t)||_rho^2, so Gronwall gives ||S0(t)||_rho <= exp(rho |t|/2) (this is 038FREE_PHASE_GROWTH). This is sufficient for the fixed-order band-then-mode identification: at each fixed epsilon,n the finite-degree multiplication bound is 2 sqrt(N+1) sqrt(v_epsilon) with v_epsilon=Gamma_epsilon(0) (not constructor V_a), the phase insertion (u,v)->(0, W_epsilon u) costs that bound divided by rho via ||A_rho^{-1/2}||_op <= 1/rho on the velocity slot, and exp(rho|t|/2) is a finite factor on the fixed horizon [0,h]; therefore each fixed Duhamel word is dominated and converges first as the band goes to infinity and then as the Gaussian modes go to infinity, with the nonuniform v_epsilon and rho confined to the identification step. mathematical_errata.original_caption: Wrote the beta<1 product as A_n B_n, losing the powers beta and 1-beta.
mathematical_errata.corrected_derivation: Set A_n=(2 x^{1/beta})^n/n! and B_n=2^{-beta n/(1-beta)}. The exact term is A_n^beta B_n^{1-beta}: A_n^beta=2^{beta n} x^n/(n!)^beta, B_n^{1-beta}=2^{-beta n}, so A_n^beta B_n^{1-beta}=x^n/(n!)^beta. For beta in (1/2,1) apply Hölder with conjugate exponents p=1/beta and q=1/(1-beta): sum A_n^beta B_n^{1-beta} <= (sum A_n)^beta (sum B_n)^{1-beta}; sum A_n=exp(2 x^{1/beta}); sum B_n=1/(1-2^{-beta/(1-beta)})<=2 because beta/(1-beta)>1 for beta>1/2, so (sum B_n)^{1-beta}<=2^{1-beta}<=2; altogether <=2 exp(2 beta x^{1/beta}) <=2 exp(3 x^{1/beta}) since 2 beta<3 for beta<3/2. For beta>=1 use the concavity bound sum a_n^beta <= (sum a_n)^beta with a_n=x^{n/beta}/n!, giving exp(beta x^{1/beta}) <= exp(3 x^{1/beta}). Check: at beta=3/4, n=1, x=1, the unpowered A_1 B_1=2*(1/8)=1/4 while A_1^beta B_1^{1-beta}=2^{3/4}*(1/8)^{1/4}=1=x^1/(1!)^beta. Norm-order exponents are beta_042=(3-alpha)/2 and gamma_043=3-alpha, so the norm-order exponent is gamma_043/2, distinct from the tail-order gamma.
